question.problem:
What is the quotient of $12{x}^{4}-5$ divided by $-2{x}^{2}+2x-3?$

The quotient is
{{field-1}}.
question.worked_solution:
Notice that the dividend is missing the ${x}^{3},{x}^{2}$ and $x$ terms. So, we first rewrite it by including the missing terms with zero coefficients, as follows:

$$
12{x}^{4}-5=12{x}^{4}+0{x}^{3}+0{x}^{2}+0x-5
$$

Now, using the method of polynomial division, we obtain the following:

$$
\begin{aligned} & \,\,\,\,\,-6{x}^{2}-6x+3 \\  & -2{x}^{2}+2x-3\,\enclose{longdiv}{\,\,12{x}^{4}+\phantom{0}0{x}^{3}+\phantom{0}0{x}^{2}+\phantom{0}0x-5\,\,} \\  & \,\,\,\,\,{12{x}^{4}-12{x}^{3}+18{x}^{2}}_{―} \\  & \,\,\,\,\,\,\,12{x}^{3}-18{x}^{2}+0x-5 \\  & \,\,\,\,\,\,\,{12{x}^{3}-12{x}^{2}+18x}_{―} \\  & \,\,\,\,\,\,-\,6{x}^{2}-18x-5 \\  & \,\,\,\,\,\,{-\,6{x}^{2}+6x-9}_{―} \\  & \,\,\,\,\,\,-\,24x+4\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, 

- the quotient is $-6{x}^{2}-6x+3,$ and

- the remainder is $-24x+4.$
